704563.t: From *ϝεμέω (*weméō), secondarily thematized from Proto-Indo-European *wémh₁ti, from *wemh₁- (“to vomit”). Cognate with Latin vomō and Sanskrit वमति (vamati).

704530.t: Possibly from Proto-Indo-European *welp- (“to hope, expect”), like ἔλπω (élpō, “to cause to hope”).

704580.t: See the etymology of the corresponding lemma form.

704578.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁mós; compare ἐμέ (emé, “me”). Cognate with Old Armenian իմ (im).

704529.t: From ἐλπίς (elpís, “hope”) + *-ϳω (*-jō). Synchronically also analyzable as ἐλπίς (elpís) + -ίζω (-ízō).

704527.t: From Proto-Hellenic *hélos, from Proto-Indo-European *sélos ~ *séles- (“marsh”). Cognate with Sanskrit सरस् (sáras) and perhaps Old Armenian եղտիւր (ełtiwr).

704508.t: The present stem is a late back-formation from εἵλκυσα (heílkŭsă), aorist tense of ἕλκω (hélkō), and εἵλκυκα (heílkŭkă), perfect tense of the same.

704507.t: From Proto-Indo-European *h₁élḱos (“wound, illness, ulcer”), from the root *h₁elḱ-. Cognate with Latin ulcus (“ulcer”) and Sanskrit अर्श॑स् (árśas, “hemorrhoids”)).

704583.t: From ἐν- (en-) + παίζω (paízō, “to play like a child”).
